review_notes: I read the whole file but did not open any related source files. The only repetition is structural. First, `SubdivisionStep.isSurfaceValid`, `isConnected` and `isGallierValid` each use the same three-way `rcases` split. `SubdivisionStep.preservesPolygonalRealization` repeats that split a fourth time. Second, `Subdivides.isSurfaceValid`, `isConnected` and `isGallierValid` use the same `ReflTransGen` induction. Each proof is only a few lines of case analysis or induction, and each leaf step is a single call to an existing lemma. That is routine case-splitting and induction over existing API. A shared generic preservation lemma would only move the duplicated branches into a helper, and the rubric says that is not enough. It would also have to be stated over arbitrary predicates and per-disjunct hypotheses, and that would be harder to read than the current short proofs. The two `polygonallyEquivalent` theorems use different arguments. `Subdivides.polygonallyEquivalent` is an induction, and `HasCommonSubdivision.polygonallyEquivalent` is a short composition of it with `trans` and `symm`. So I found no nontrivial reasoning repeated across proofs. The only remaining uncertainty is whether a maintainer would still want to factor out the three parallel validity-preservation proofs. I judged that cosmetic.
